summary: Krishnanath Chatterjee was an Indology scholar who studied under Surendra Nath Bhattacharya, Haripada Chakravarty, Ramaranjan Mukherji, Krishna Gopal Goswami, Satkari Mookerjee, Amarasvar Thakur, and Siddheshwar Bhattacharya.

Krishnaswamy Nachimuthu is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. In 2021, he held a post at the École Française d'Extrême-Orient and served on the editorial board of Studies on the History of Śaivism.

Kristin Johnston Largen is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. In 2018, she was Professor of Systematic Theology at United Lutheran Seminary and Associate Dean of Religious and Spiritual Life at Gettysburg College.

Kristin Scheible works in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned a BA from Colby College and an MTS from Harvard (2006), studying under Anne E. Monius, Diana L. Eck, John S. Strong, and Charles Hallisey. She taught at Harvard, Brown, and Bard College (attested 2008).

Kristina Myrvold works in religious studies and Indology. She was an editor (2005) and PhD candidate (2008) at Lund University, and became Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at Linnaeus University (attested 2014).

Kristofer Schipper (1934–2021) was a sinologist and religious studies scholar. Educated at Paris Diderot, EPHE, and INALCO, he held posts at EFEO (~1962–1973), EPHE (1972–2002), Collège de France (1987–1992), and Leiden (1993–1999).

Krisztina Teleki (born 1978) specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. She earned an MA at Eötvös Loránd University (~1996–2009), where she later served as a research fellow (~2011).
Kshanika Saha is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed her PhD at the University of Calcutta (attested 1966) under the instruction of Nalinaksha Dutt.

Kshetresa Chandra Chattopadhyaya (1896–1974) studied linguistics and Indology under Ganganatha Jha at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Calcutta University. He taught at the University of Allahabad (from 1924) and directed the Research Institute at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1957–1965).

Kshitimohan Sen (1880–1960) was an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University. After working in Chamba State (~1903–1908), he joined Visva-Bharati University in 1908 and served as Adhyaksha there from 1953 to 1954.
Kumar Shrestha is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. In 2018, he was affiliated with the National Archives of Nepal and served as an editorial board member for Documenta Nepalica.

Kumataro Kawada (1899–1981) was a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who earned his doctorate at the University of Tokyo in 1941. He taught at Japan Women's University, Tokyo University of Literature and Science, the University of Tokyo (1950–1959), and Komazawa University.

Kun Chang (1917–2017) was a linguist, sinologist, and tibetologist educated at Tsinghua and Yale under Franklin Edgerton and Geshe Ngawang Nyima. He held posts at Academia Sinica, the University of Washington, and UC Berkeley (1963–1987).

Kunio Harikai (born 1942) is an Indology and philosophy scholar who earned his degrees at Kyushu University under Seiren Matsunami and Shoren Ihara. He held posts at Saga University (~1976–1990) and Saga Medical School (~1990–1998).
Kunio Iwaya (born 1943) studied at the University of Tokyo (~1961–1967) and held a post at Meiji Gakuin University from approximately 1974 to 2014.
Kunio Mugitani (born 1948) is a sinology and philosophy scholar who studied under Mitsuji Fukunaga. He served as a professor at Kyoto University from approximately 1993 to 2013.
Kunio Odaka (1908–1993) studied at the University of Tokyo (~1928–1931). He later held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1947–1969) and Sophia University (~1969–1979).

Kunio Yanagita (1875–1962), a scholar of Japanology and religious studies, studied law at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at the Ministry of Agriculture and Commerce, Tokyo Asahi Shimbun, the Permanent Mandates Commission, Keio University, and Kokugakuin University.

Kuno Fischer (1824–1907) was a philosopher who studied at the universities of Leipzig and Halle-Wittenberg. He held faculty posts at the University of Jena (~1856–1872) and the University of Heidelberg (~1872–1906).

Kuno Lorenz (born 1932) is a philosopher who studied at Tübingen, Hamburg, Bonn, Princeton, Kiel (PhD), and Erlangen-Nürnberg. He held a chair in philosophy at the University of Hamburg (1970) and was a professor at Saarland University (1974–1998).
